key_insight: Raising the flame-spraying O₂/C₂H₂ ratio densified Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings, lowering porosity and roughness while improving adhesion, with peak microhardness at 1.1.
engineering_relevance: Process-gas tuning provides a practical lever to optimize flame-sprayed coating quality for wear- and corrosion-resistant surfaces on AISI 321 steel.
method: Flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si coatings onto AISI 321 stainless steel using a Metal Coat 6PM-II system.
Varied the O₂/C₂H₂ ratio to 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 while monitoring spray conditions with Accuraspray 4.0.
Measured microstructure, porosity, microhardness, surface roughness, and adhesion strength.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports porosity dropping from 1.97 ± 0.13% to 0.90 ± 0.09%, roughness from 4.70 ± 0.09 μm to 2.99 ± 0.11 μm, adhesion rising from 22.14 ± 4.3 MPa to 35.02 ± 3.9 MPa, and maximum hardness of 1051.7 HV at O₂/C₂H₂ = 1.1.
watch_item: The best adhesion/lowest porosity occurred at the highest gas ratio, but the microhardness optimum differed, so selecting a single setting depends on whether toughness, hardness, or bonding is the priority.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
